identity.name: Belrise Industries Ltd
identity.industry: Auto components — metal/chassis & safety systems (+ emerging aerospace/defense precision mfg)

summary.oneLiner: Belrise is a diversified 2W/3W metal & plastics leader (exhaust, fuel tanks, chassis) compounding via three levers: rising content-per-vehicle (2W ~INR12k→20k over 18 months, +60-65%), proprietary segment wins (suspensions, steering columns, high-tensile, braking), and a cheap-multiple M&A strategy now opening a high-complexity aerospace/defense leg aimed at India localization. Back-to-back RM pricing protects gross margins; FY26 delivered guided mid-teens growth with stable margins.

thesis: Belrise is a diversified 2W/3W metal & plastics leader (exhaust, fuel tanks, chassis) compounding via three levers: rising content-per-vehicle (2W ~INR12k→20k over 18 months, +60-65%), proprietary segment wins (suspensions, steering columns, high-tensile, braking), and a cheap-multiple M&A strategy now opening a high-complexity aerospace/defense leg aimed at India localization. Back-to-back RM pricing protects gross margins; FY26 delivered guided mid-teens growth with stable margins.
scorecard: Segment mix (mfg, FY26): 2W/3W 82.0%, PV 5.2%, CV 8.3%, others 4.5%. Q4: 2W/3W 83.2%, PV 6.2%, CV 8.4%, others 2.2%. FY26 4W segment +37%, CV +35%; Q4 4W +71%, CV +32%.
guidance: EBITDA margins broadly stable vs FY26 levels.
Capex 6%–6.5% of manufacturing revenue (R&D included within this).
Double 4W+CV business over 2 years; needs ~40-45% growth vs FY25 base this fiscal.
Belrise SDM expected EBITDA-positive in CY2027 (one-time INR94.7mn startup loss in Q4 not recurring).
Aerospace targeted to grow into a >10% revenue contributor over time.
order book / new wins: 2W/3W OEM (fastest-growing): new order for exhaust systems + fuel tanks for top-selling model; Bangalore brownfield, production from Q2 FY27, peak revenue ~INR90 cr. Built from earlier steering-column + suspension programs (broke 3-decade monopoly on steering columns).

Japanese 2W OEM: 8-week rescue of distressed Tier-1 led to large order for complete exhaust systems + metal components for highest-selling model; peak ~INR220 cr (~INR2,000mn), production from Q4 FY27. (Combined #1+#2 = ~INR310 cr peak.)
Haridwar facility ramping; trial parts dispatched to largest 2W OEM; fed by Greater Noida & Pantnagar (backward integration, limited greenfield capex).
Chassis wins for new marquee model launches at a top customer's Pune & Sambhajinagar plants (partly replacement).
EV: chassis, battery trays + metal components for an emerging EV player (in partnership with a large Japanese 2W OEM); supplies from Q3 FY27.
Premium export: single-source component order for a 650cc Italian OEM premium motorbike (low volume, high complexity, only one other domestic supplier capable).
Proprietary segment marquee customer adds: suspensions +4, steering columns +4, high-tensile +4, braking +2.
segment: 2W/3W dominant (~82% mfg rev) and structurally favored — segment only just regained pre-COVID peak, leaving headroom. 4W/CV small but blue-ocean, growing fast (H-One lifted 4W content INR25k→40-45k). Aerospace/defense nascent but strategic, built entirely via M&A (SDM France + Chester Hall UK). Trading business is margin-dilutive; possible localization/hive-off discussed but no decision.
growth drivers: Content-per-vehicle expansion (2W +60-65%, of which ~80% proprietary in-house products) + cross-selling each new product to 3-4 OEMs.
New 2W OEM penetration (two large fast-growers from near-zero base → "very large" in 2-3 yrs).
4W/CV model wins via H-One high-tensile (up to 1,200 MPa domestic / 1,700 MPa via H-One global) enabling lightweighting & safety.
GST rate cut demand stimulus (hope structural, not pull-forward).
Aerospace India localization (China+1, captive Indian aircraft demand, 8-11 yr aircraft backlogs, certification moats acquired via M&A).
margins: EBITDA 11.4% (Q4) / 12.1% (FY26); mfg EBITDA 13.0% / 13.7%. Back-to-back RM pricing (steel, plastic) passes input cost moves to customers with a lag → stable gross margins. Q4 pressured by one-time INR94.7mn SDM startup loss + acquisition legal/professional fees + oil-crisis-driven fuel/transport/labor/personnel costs (Haryana min-wage). Fuel & labor to be passed on over time; transport still under OEM discussion. Mgmt expects no material medium/long-term margin impact.
capex: 6%–6.5% of manufacturing revenue (R&D included). Capex % has risen and expected to keep rising as products get more sophisticated. R&D team 163 people across suspensions, steering, high-tensile, braking; new products in 12-18 month pipeline. Brownfield-led expansion (Bangalore, Haridwar) to limit greenfield spend.
capital allocation: M&A discipline: targets chosen on customers / capabilities / verticalization; pay "mild" multiples. Mag Filter & SDM at ~book value; Chester Hall & H-One at mid-single-digit EV/EBITDA. All four EPS- and ROCE-accretive from day one.
QIP: enabling resolution up to INR2,000 cr (purpose not yet specified — debt repay / acquisition TBD).
Merger of Badve Autocomps & Eximius into listco at ~book value (group simplification).
Final dividend INR0.55/share. Net debt INR5,977mn; ROCE 14.7%.
risks: Oil-crisis cost inflation (fuel, transport, labor, personnel); Haryana minimum-wage hike — pass-through partial/lagged, transport unresolved.
Commodity volatility (mitigated by back-to-back pricing but with lag).
Aerospace execution: SDM startup losses, long certification lead times (12-24 months), integration risk.
Customer concentration legacy (historically single-customer dependent; now diversified).
Chassis wins partly cannibalize existing business.
QIP dilution risk (up to INR2,000 cr, undefined use).
mgmt tone: Confident and delivery-focused; emphasized hitting all five FY26 commitments. Candid on Q4 cost headwinds but framed as one-time/short-term. Declined plant-level utilization/break-even, segment-level revenue (suspension/polymer, H-One), and QIP use specifics — guarded on granular numbers.
non-obvious: Steering column was a 3-decade single-supplier monopoly Belrise broke via engineering — the wedge that won the fastest-growing 2W/3W OEM.
Stainless-steel surface-coating/plating for premium exhausts is a near-unique domestic capability (competitive moat).
850+ robots fleet + full verticalization (tooling→stamping→fabrication→painting/coating→assembly) underpins exhaust cost edge.
Aerospace M&A is really about buying certifications/customer access (otherwise 2-3 yr + 12-24 month qualification) to then shift work to India ("best-cost," not low-cost).
Chester Hall: GBP18.5mn rev, GBP2.1mn EBITDA, >20% ROCE, single-source reverse-thruster/nacelle parts, top-5 quality at engine OEM, titanium/Al-grade-7 machining, 0.5-1% rejection.
Content-per-vehicle INR20k figure includes the Badve Autocomps + Eximius merger.
qoq change log: First structured note for BELRISE in this system (FY26 = first full year post-May-2025 IPO). Baseline established. Key new-this-quarter items: Chester Hall UK acquisition closed (Q4 FY26); SDM one-time INR94.7mn startup loss; QIP enabling resolution up to INR2,000 cr announced; Badve Autocomps + Eximius merger Board-approved; new 2W exhaust/fuel-tank orders (~INR310 cr combined peak); EV chassis/battery-tray order; 650cc Italian export single-source win. Compare against next quarter.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
